subject.title: [Bug] Webchat avatar endpoint /avatar/{agentId} returns 404 even with valid IDENTITY.md avatar

question: Should local avatar failures keep the direct image route generic while improving UI/metadata diagnostics, or should `/avatar/{agentId}` expose more specific failure statuses such as oversized or missing?
rationale: The remaining change affects diagnostics for authenticated local workspace file serving, so automation should not choose the information-disclosure and UX tradeoff on its own.

options.title: Improve UI Diagnostics Only
options.body: Keep direct image fetches generic and use the metadata route plus Control UI copy to explain missing, oversized, unsupported, or outside-workspace avatars.

options.title: Expose Endpoint Errors
options.body: Return specific direct-route statuses such as 413 or 400 after maintainer security review accepts the information-disclosure tradeoff.

options.title: Fold Into Broader Avatar Contract
options.body: Track the remaining work in the broader Control UI avatar issue if maintainers want one unified avatar policy decision.

recommendation.title: Improve UI Diagnostics Only
recommendation.body: Keep direct image fetches generic and use the metadata route plus Control UI copy to explain missing, oversized, unsupported, or outside-workspace avatars.

likelyOwner.reason: This person has the strongest history signal for both the original avatar feature and the later local file-serving safety policy.
